title: Module 10 intro — Safety, Ethics, and Compliance

lines: Welcome to Module Ten: Safety, Ethics, and Compliance.
Alignment makes a model usually behave; this module makes sure it does.
Picture a travel company's booking assistant that reads web pages and calls tools.
In its first week, three things go wrong.
First, a user role-plays the bot into writing content it should refuse.
That's a jailbreak: attacking the model's own safety policy.
Second, a hotel page hides white text telling the bot to leak customer details.
That's indirect prompt injection, and the user was completely innocent.
Third, a customer's passport number turns up in the logs.
Nobody meant to store it, and nothing stopped it.
A system-prompt line saying "ignore injected instructions" fixes none of this.
The fix is architecture: guardrails that check what goes in and what comes out.
Lesson one builds those guardrails with NeMo Guardrails.
Input, dialog, retrieval, execution and output rails each catch different failures.

say.0: Lesson one builds those guardrails with nemo Guardrails.

lines: Safety classifiers like Llama Guard and NemoGuard label each turn safe or unsafe.
Colang flows keep conversations on topic, and tool calls need allow-lists.

say.1: Coe-lang flows keep conversations on topic, and tool calls need allow-lists.

lines: PII is masked before it reaches the model, the answer or the logs.
And because every rail adds latency, you'll layer defences that stay fast.

lines: Lesson two turns to responsible AI, starting with bias.
Swap only the name on identical CVs, and see whether the hiring advice changes.

lines: Counterfactual tests, fairness metrics and benchmarks like BBQ turn a worry into a number.
Mitigations then span data, training, inference and monitoring.

lines: Next comes red teaming: attacking your own system before anyone else does.
Scanners like garak fire thousands of probes, and humans find the creative failures.

say.1: Scanners like gah-rack fire thousands of probes, and humans find the creative failures.

lines: Every model ships with a model card: intended use, limits, and results by group.
And licenses follow the weights and data into your fine-tune.
Regulation depends on how a model is used.
Under the EU AI Act, a writing helper is limited risk, but screening job applicants is high risk.

say.1: Under the E U A I Act, a writing helper is limited risk, but screening job applicants is high risk.

lines: So compliance is monitored continuously: guardrail blocks, refusals and outcomes by group.
And every model or prompt change triggers a fresh audit.
By the end, you'll wrap an LLM in guardrails, audit it for bias, red-team it, and document it.
Let's start with lesson one: guardrails.
